blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Transfer learning typically reuses knowledge acquired by a source network through its learned weights. We investigate whether a learned activation function can also be transferred and remain useful in networks trained from scratch. We study this complementary form of transfer through a learn-freeze-transfer protocol, in which the activation is optimized jointly with a source network in a single training run, and is then frozen and reused in target networks trained from scratch. A pointwise activation with globally shared parameters is independent of layer dimensions and can therefore be incorporated into networks of different architectures trained from scratch. We instantiate this protocol with FAct, a five-parameter activation represented by a two-harmonic truncated Fourier series, initialized from a Fourier approximation of GELU and learned in a Vision Transformer (ViT) on ImageNet-1K. When reused in a ViT of the same architecture trained from scratch on ImageNet-1K, the frozen activation (Frozen FAct) improves top-1 accuracy by 1.46 percentage points over GELU. Across four smaller target architectures (standard ViT, Swin Transformer, linear-attention ViT, and MLP-Mixer) and four image-classification datasets, it achieves the highest mean accuracy among eleven activation functions in 15 of 16 settings under a common training configuration, with improvements of up to 1.71 percentage points over the best conventional activation. When the learning rate and weight decay are tuned separately for each activation under the same search budget, Frozen FAct still ranks first in 11 of the 16 settings, second in four, and fourth in one. These results provide empirical evidence that a learned activation function can retain its usefulness when transferred across vision architectures, independently of the weights with which it was learned.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Transfer learning typically reuses knowledge acquired by a source network through its learned weights.
We investigate whether an activation function learned jointly with a source network in a single training
run can also be transferred to target networks and remain useful. To this end, we
use a parameterized activation function whose coefficients are shared globally across all activation
sites of the network. Global sharing makes the number of activation parameters independent of network
depth and width, so the learned function can be reused in networks of different architectures. This
yields a complementary form of transfer, in which the learned activation, rather than the source-network
weights, is retained and reused.

to examine whether a nonlinearity learned within one network remains useful across different

blocks.en: This work makes three contributions:
blocks.zh: 这项工作有三项贡献:

blocks.en:
1. A learn–freeze–transfer protocol for activation functions. We formulate a complementary
form of transfer in which a globally shared activation is learned jointly with a source network in a
single training run, then frozen and reused in target networks trained from scratch, without
transferring source-network weights. 2. A globally shared activation suited for transfer. We instantiate the protocol with
FAct, whose five coefficients are shared across all MLP blocks, so that the learned activation can be
placed in networks of different architectures. 3. An empirical evaluation of activation transferability. We evaluate same-task and
cross-architecture transfer using three transformer architectures and an attention-free MLP-Mixer on
four image-classification datasets. We compare Frozen FAct with ten conventional activation functions under
common and activation-specific hyperparameter configurations, and we include a control showing that the
gains come from the learned activation rather than its parameterization.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Transfer Learning
blocks.zh: 2.1 转移学习

blocks.en:
Transfer learning reuses knowledge acquired on a source task to improve learning on a target
task [ 28 ] . In deep networks, this is typically done by reusing learned weights, either
to initialize a target network that is then fine-tuned or as fixed feature
extractors [ 37 ] . Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge between networks
of different architectures, but it requires the source network during target training to provide
supervision [ 12 ] . In both cases, the transferred knowledge is carried by the
source network’s weights or outputs. We study a complementary setting in which only a learned activation
function is transferred, and the source network is not used during target training.

任务[28]。 在深层网络中,通常通过重用学到的重量来完成。

源网络的权重或输出。 我们研究一个互补的环境,在这个环境里,只有学习到的激活
函数被转移,而源网络在目标训练中不使用。

blocks.en: 2.2 Learnable and Globally Shared Activation Functions
blocks.zh: 2.2 可学习和全球共享的活动职能

blocks.en:
Learnable activation functions introduce parameterized nonlinear transformations whose parameters are
optimized jointly with the network weights. PReLU learns the slope of the negative input
region [ 10 ] , and ACON provides a more flexible parametric
formulation [ 23 ] . Padé activation units represent the nonlinearity as a ratio of
polynomials [ 26 ] , while other approaches use adaptive piecewise-linear
functions [ 1 ] or kernel-based representations [ 30 ] .
Learnable Fourier-type activations have also been studied, with coefficients learned within the network
in which they are used [ 17 , 19 , 31 ] .

与网络权重联合优化. PRELU 学习负输入的斜率
区域[10],和ACON提供更灵活的参数
[23]。 Padé激活单位代表非线性比

blocks.en:
Activation parameters also differ in how they are shared. They may be assigned to individual neurons or
layers, or shared across multiple layers. Jagtap et al. [14] introduced globally adaptive activation
functions for deep and physics-informed neural networks, using a single trainable scaling parameter that
adjusts the activation slope across the network. Delfosse et al. [5] shared a common set of
rational-function parameters across layers to regulate activation plasticity in deep reinforcement
learning. These approaches show that sharing activation parameters within a network can be useful.
However, sharing alone does not show whether a learned activation can be separated from its source
network and reused in another network.

然而,单靠分享并不能表明是否可以将所学的激活与其来源分开
在另一个网络中重新使用。

blocks.en: 2.3 Reuse and Transfer of Activation Functions
blocks.zh: 2.3 激活功能的再使用和转让

blocks.en:
Several studies have reused activation functions beyond the setting in which they were obtained. Ramachandran et al. [29] discovered Swish by automated search on a small network and showed that it
transfers to larger models and other tasks. Bingham and Miikkulainen [2] used surrogate-based search to
find activation functions that transfer from small search tasks to larger models, including ResNet-50 on
ImageNet. Strack et al. [32] used gradient-based search and transferred the resulting activations,
with their constants fixed, to larger models of the same type and to new datasets. Teney et al. [34] meta-learned activation functions through bilevel optimization across task
episodes, demonstrating transfer across algorithmic tasks and reuse in networks of different widths.
blocks.zh:
一些研究在获得活化功能的设定之外再利用这些功能。 拉玛昌德兰等. [29] 在一个小网络上通过自动搜索发现了Swish,并显示它
转让给更大的模型和其他任务。 Bingham和Miikkulainen [2] 使用基于替代的搜索方式
找到将小搜索任务转移到更大模型的激活功能,包括 ResNet-50 上

和新的数据集。 特尼等人著. [34] 通过全任务双层优化获得元a激活功能
实例,演示跨算法任务的转移和不同宽度的网络中的再利用。

blocks.en:
Reusing a learned shape does not always preserve its benefit. Tavakoli et al. [33] found that a
fixed activation mimicking the final shape of trained SPLASH units performed only on par with ReLU, and
concluded that the evolution of the shape during training was important. Although this was not a transfer
study, it suggests that freezing a learned activation may discard part of its benefit.

blocks.en:
The present study differs from these works in two respects. First, the activation is learned in a single
conventional training run, without search or meta-learning. Second, the frozen coefficients are
transferred across architecture families, from a ViT to Swin, linear-attention, and MLP-Mixer targets,
without reusing source-network weights or updating the activation during target training.

blocks.en: 3 FAct: Learning and Transferring a Shared Nonlinearity
blocks.zh: 3 FAct:学习和转让共享的非线性

blocks.en: 3.1 Global Activation Sharing
blocks.zh: 3.1 全球活动共享

blocks.en: 4 Experimental Evaluation
blocks.zh: 4 实验评价.

blocks.en:
This section evaluates whether a globally shared activation learned jointly with a source network
remains useful when transferred to independently initialized target networks. We first describe the
source and target architectures, datasets, and training protocol. We then examine the evolution of the
source-learned activation, its transfer to a network with the same architecture and task, and its
transfer across four target architectures with different attention and token-mixing mechanisms.
Frozen FAct is compared with ten conventional activation functions to assess its performance under a
common training configuration.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
This work investigated whether a globally shared activation learned jointly with a source network can
be reused independently of the network weights with which it was optimized. We introduced a
learn–freeze–transfer framework and instantiated it using FAct, a five-parameter activation
represented by a two-harmonic truncated Fourier series. Initialized using a Fourier approximation of
GELU, its coefficients are optimized jointly with a source Vision Transformer and subsequently frozen
for transfer to independently initialized target networks.
blocks.zh:
这项工作调查了与源网络共同学习的全球共享激活能否
与优化时的网络重量无关。 我们介绍了一个
学习- 冻结- 传输框架, 并使用 FAct, 五参数激活

GELU,它的系数与源视觉变换器一起优化,然后被冻结
用于向独立初始化的目标网络转移。

blocks.en:
We evaluated the proposed approach through same-task and cross-architecture transfer experiments. In the
same-task setting, Frozen FAct improved ImageNet-1K top-1 accuracy by 1.46 1.46 percentage points over GELU
when used in a freshly initialized ViT-d6. Across four target architectures and four
image-classification datasets, Frozen FAct achieved the highest mean test accuracy among eleven activation
choices in 15 of the 16 architecture–dataset combinations under a common training configuration. This
included all twelve combinations involving the three transformer architectures and three of four
MLP-Mixer combinations. Following activation-specific hyperparameter tuning, Frozen FAct ranked first in
eleven combinations, second in four, and fourth in the remaining combination. Throughout these
experiments, only the five learned activation coefficients were transferred; source-network weights
were not reused, and the activation remained fixed during target training.

blocks.en:
These findings provide empirical evidence that a globally shared nonlinearity learned within one network
can retain its usefulness when transferred to independently initialized networks with different
architectures and target tasks. However, the evaluation uses a single source-learned activation obtained
from one Vision Transformer trained on ImageNet-1K, and the cross-architecture experiments are
restricted to relatively small target networks and image-classification tasks. Further investigation is
needed to establish how activation transferability varies across source architectures, source training
datasets, model scales, and target tasks. Extending this evaluation to convolutional and other network
architectures would help determine the broader applicability of transferable learned nonlinearities.
The mechanism behind the gains also remains open.

blocks.en:
We first compare Frozen GELU-init with GELU to examine whether the fixed Fourier approximation alone

improvements observed with Frozen FAct.
